sanskrit: ajñaś cāśraddadhānaś ca saṃśayātmā vinaśyati nāyaṃ loko 'sti na paro na sukhaṃ saṃśayātmanaḥ
english: The ignorant one, devoid of faith, whose very self is doubt, comes to ruin; for the doubting soul there is neither this world nor the world beyond, nor any happiness.

sanskrit: yogasaṃnyastakarmāṇaṃ jñānasaṃchinnasaṃśayam ātmavantaṃ na karmāṇi nibadhnanti dhanaṃjaya
english: The one who has renounced action through yoga, whose doubt has been severed by knowledge, who is possessed of the self—such a one, O Dhanaṃjaya, actions do not bind.

sanskrit: tasmād ajñānasaṃbhūtaṃ hṛtsthaṃ jñānāsinātmanaḥ chittvainaṃ saṃśayaṃ yogam ātiṣṭhottiṣṭha bhārata
english: Therefore, having cut away with the sword of knowledge this doubt born of ignorance that dwells in your heart, take your stand in yoga, and rise up, O Bhārata!

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca saṃnyāsaṃ karmaṇāṃ kṛṣṇa punar yogaṃ ca śaṃsasi yac chreya etayor ekaṃ tan me brūhi suniścitam
english: Arjuna said: You praise the renunciation of actions, O Kṛṣṇa, and again you praise yoga. Tell me with full certainty which one of these two is the better.

sanskrit: śrībhagavān uvāca saṃnyāsaḥ karmayogaś ca niḥśreyasakarāv ubhau tayos tu karmasaṃnyāsāt karmayogo viśiṣyate
english: The Blessed Lord said: Both renunciation and the yoga of action lead to the highest good; yet of the two, the yoga of action is more excellent than the renunciation of action.

sanskrit: jñeyaḥ sa nityasaṃnyāsī yo na dveṣṭi na kāṅkṣati nirdvaṃdvo hi mahābāho sukhaṃ bandhāt pramucyate
english: He is to be known as the perpetual renouncer who neither hates nor craves; for the one free from the pairs of opposites, O mighty-armed, is easily released from bondage.

sanskrit: sāṃkhyayogau pṛthag bālāḥ pravadanti na paṇḍitāḥ ekam apy āsthitaḥ samyag ubhayor vindate phalam
english: It is children, not the wise, who speak of Sāṃkhya and yoga as distinct; one who is rightly established in even one of them gains the fruit of both.

sanskrit: yat sāṃkhyaiḥ prāpyate sthānaṃ tad yogair api gamyate ekaṃ sāṃkhyaṃ ca yogaṃ ca yaḥ paśyati sa paśyati
english: The state that is attained by the followers of Sāṃkhya is reached by the yogins as well; he who sees Sāṃkhya and yoga as one, he truly sees.

sanskrit: saṃnyāsas tu mahābāho duḥkham āptum ayogataḥ yogayukto munir brahma nacireṇādhigacchati
english: But renunciation, O mighty-armed, is hard to attain without yoga; the sage yoked in yoga reaches Brahman before long.

sanskrit: yogayukto viśuddhātmā vijitātmā jitendriyaḥ sarvabhūtātmabhūtātmā kurvann api na lipyate
english: Yoked in yoga, of purified self, his self mastered and his senses conquered, his self become the self of all beings—though he acts, he is not stained.

sanskrit: naiva kiṃ cit karomīti yukto manyeta tattvavit paśyañ śṛṇvan spṛśañ jighrann aśnan gacchan svapañ śvasan
english: "I do nothing at all"—so should the yoked one, the knower of truth, think, even while seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, eating, walking, sleeping, breathing,

sanskrit: pralapan visṛjan gṛhṇann unmiṣan nimiṣann api indriyāṇīndriyārtheṣu vartanta iti dhārayan
english: speaking, releasing, grasping, opening and closing his eyes—holding fast to the truth that it is the senses alone that move among the objects of the senses.

sanskrit: brahmaṇy ādhāya karmāṇi saṅgaṃ tyaktvā karoti yaḥ lipyate na sa pāpena padmapatram ivāmbhasā
english: He who acts, surrendering his actions to Brahman and abandoning attachment, is untouched by evil, as a lotus leaf is untouched by water.

sanskrit: kāyena manasā buddhyā kevalair indriyair api yoginaḥ karma kurvanti saṅgaṃ tyaktvātmaśuddhaye
english: With the body, the mind, the intellect, and the senses alone, the yogins perform action, abandoning attachment, for the purification of the self.

sanskrit: yuktaḥ karmaphalaṃ tyaktvā śāntim āpnoti naiṣṭhikīm ayuktaḥ kāmakāreṇa phale sakto nibadhyate
english: The yoked one, having abandoned the fruit of action, attains lasting peace; the unyoked one, driven by desire and attached to the fruit, is bound.

sanskrit: sarvakarmāṇi manasā saṃnyasyāste sukhaṃ vaśī navadvāre pure dehī naiva kurvan na kārayan
english: Renouncing all actions with the mind, the master of himself, the embodied one rests happily in the city of nine gates, neither acting nor causing to act.

sanskrit: na kartṛtvaṃ na karmāṇi lokasya sṛjati prabhuḥ na karmaphalasaṃyogaṃ svabhāvas tu pravartate
english: The Lord creates for the world neither agency nor actions, nor the union of action with its fruit; it is inherent nature that takes its course.

sanskrit: nādatte kasya cit pāpaṃ na caiva sukṛtaṃ vibhuḥ ajñānenāvṛtaṃ jñānaṃ tena muhyanti jantavaḥ
english: The all-pervading one takes on no one's evil deed, nor indeed any good deed; knowledge is veiled by ignorance, and by this creatures are deluded.

sanskrit: jñānena tu tad ajñānaṃ yeṣāṃ nāśitam ātmanaḥ teṣām ādityavaj jñānaṃ prakāśayati tatparam
english: But for those whose ignorance of the self has been destroyed by knowledge, their knowledge, like the sun, illumines that Supreme.

sanskrit: tadbuddhayas tadātmānas tanniṣṭhās tatparāyaṇāḥ gacchanty apunarāvṛttiṃ jñānanirdhūtakalmaṣāḥ
english: With their understanding fixed on That, their self in That, established in That, holding That as their supreme goal, they go to that from which there is no return, their stains shaken off by knowledge.

sanskrit: vidyāvinayasaṃpanne brāhmaṇe gavi hastini śuni caiva śvapāke ca paṇḍitāḥ samadarśinaḥ
english: In a brāhmaṇa endowed with learning and humility, in a cow, in an elephant, and in a dog, and even in one who eats the flesh of dogs, the wise see the same.

sanskrit: ihaiva tair jitaḥ sargo yeṣāṃ sāmye sthitaṃ manaḥ nirdoṣaṃ hi samaṃ brahma tasmād brahmaṇi te sthitāḥ
english: Even here the round of birth is conquered by those whose mind is established in equanimity; for Brahman is flawless and the same in all, and therefore they abide in Brahman.

sanskrit: na prahṛṣyet priyaṃ prāpya nodvijet prāpya cāpriyam sthirabuddhir asaṃmūḍho brahmavid brahmaṇi sthitaḥ
english: He would not rejoice on gaining what is pleasant, nor shudder on gaining what is unpleasant—steady of understanding, undeluded, the knower of Brahman, established in Brahman.

sanskrit: bāhyasparśeṣv asaktātmā vindaty ātmani yat sukham sa brahmayogayuktātmā sukham akṣayam aśnute
english: With his self unattached to outward contacts, he finds the happiness that lies within the self; with his self yoked in union with Brahman, he enjoys imperishable happiness.

sanskrit: ye hi saṃsparśajā bhogā duḥkhayonaya eva te ādyantavantaḥ kaunteya na teṣu ramate budhaḥ
english: For the enjoyments born of contact are wombs of pain alone; they have a beginning and an end, O son of Kuntī, and the wise man does not delight in them.

sanskrit: śaknotīhaiva yaḥ soḍhuṃ prāk śarīravimokṣaṇāt kāmakrodhodbhavaṃ vegaṃ sa yuktaḥ sa sukhī naraḥ
english: He who is able, here in this very life, before he is freed from the body, to withstand the surge born of desire and anger—he is yoked, he is the happy man.

sanskrit: yo 'ntaḥsukho 'ntarārāmas tathāntarjyotir eva yaḥ sa yogī brahmanirvāṇaṃ brahmabhūto 'dhigacchati
english: He whose happiness is within, whose delight is within, whose light too is within—that yogin, having become Brahman, attains the extinction that is Brahman.

sanskrit: labhante brahmanirvāṇam ṛṣayaḥ kṣīṇakalmaṣāḥ chinnadvaidhā yatātmānaḥ sarvabhūtahite ratāḥ
english: The seers whose stains are worn away attain the extinction that is Brahman—their dualities cut away, their selves controlled, rejoicing in the welfare of all beings.

sanskrit: kāmakrodhaviyuktānāṃ yatīnāṃ yatacetasām abhito brahmanirvāṇaṃ vartate viditātmanām
english: For the ascetics freed from desire and anger, their minds controlled, who have come to know the self, the extinction that is Brahman is present on every side.

sanskrit: sparśān kṛtvā bahir bāhyāṃś cakṣuś caivāntare bhruvoḥ prāṇāpānau samau kṛtvā nāsābhyantaracāriṇau
english: Shutting out external contacts, fixing the gaze between the brows, making even the inward and outward breaths that move within the nostrils,

sanskrit: yatendriyamanobuddhir munir mokṣaparāyaṇaḥ vigatecchābhayakrodho yaḥ sadā mukta eva saḥ
english: the sage whose senses, mind, and intellect are restrained, intent on liberation, from whom desire, fear, and anger have departed—he is forever truly free.

sanskrit: bhoktāraṃ yajñatapasāṃ sarvalokamaheśvaram suhṛdaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ jñātvā māṃ śāntim ṛcchati
english: Knowing Me as the enjoyer of sacrifices and austerities, the great Lord of all the worlds, the friend of all beings, one attains peace.

sanskrit: śrībhagavān uvāca anāśritaḥ karmaphalaṃ kāryaṃ karma karoti yaḥ sa saṃnyāsī ca yogī ca na niragnir na cākriyaḥ
english: The Blessed Lord said: He who performs the work that ought to be done without depending on its fruit—he is both a renouncer and a yogin, not the one who is without sacred fire and without rites.

sanskrit: yaṃ saṃnyāsam iti prāhur yogaṃ taṃ viddhi pāṇḍava na hy asaṃnyastasaṃkalpo yogī bhavati kaś cana
english: That which they call renunciation, know that to be yoga, O Pāṇḍava; for no one becomes a yogin who has not renounced his selfish purposes.

sanskrit: ārurukṣor muner yogaṃ karma kāraṇam ucyate yogārūḍhasya tasyaiva śamaḥ kāraṇam ucyate
english: For the sage who wishes to ascend to yoga, action is said to be the means; for that same one who has ascended to yoga, serenity is said to be the means.

sanskrit: yadā hi nendriyārtheṣu na karmasv anuṣajjate sarvasaṃkalpasaṃnyāsī yogārūḍhas tadocyate
english: For when one clings neither to the objects of the senses nor to actions, having renounced all selfish intentions, then he is said to have ascended to yoga.

sanskrit: uddhared ātmanātmānaṃ nātmānam avasādayet ātmaiva hy ātmano bandhur ātmaiva ripur ātmanaḥ
english: Let a man lift up the self by the self, and not let the self sink down; for the self alone is the friend of the self, and the self alone is the enemy of the self.

sanskrit: bandhur ātmātmanas tasya yenātmaivātmanā jitaḥ anātmanas tu śatrutve vartetātmaiva śatruvat
english: For him who has conquered the self by the self, the self is the friend of the self; but for one without self-mastery, the self alone abides in enmity, like a foe.

sanskrit: jitātmanaḥ praśāntasya paramātmā samāhitaḥ śītoṣṇasukhaduḥkheṣu tathā mānāvamānayoḥ
english: For one of conquered self, who is tranquil, the supreme Self stays steadfast amid cold and heat, pleasure and pain, and likewise in honor and dishonor.

sanskrit: jñānavijñānatṛptātmā kūṭastho vijitendriyaḥ yukta ity ucyate yogī samaloṣṭāśmakāñcanaḥ
english: He whose self is content with knowledge and discernment, who stands unmoved on the summit, whose senses are conquered, to whom a clod, a stone, and gold are alike—such a yogin is called yoked.

sanskrit: suhṛnmitrāryudāsīnamadhyasthadveṣyabandhuṣu sādhuṣv api ca pāpeṣu samabuddhir viśiṣyate
english: He whose understanding is the same toward well-wisher, friend, and foe, toward the indifferent, the neutral, the hateful, and the kinsman, and toward the good and the wicked alike—he is the most excellent.

sanskrit: yogī yuñjīta satatam ātmānaṃ rahasi sthitaḥ ekākī yatacittātmā nirāśīr aparigrahaḥ
english: Let the yogin ever yoke himself, abiding in a secret place, alone, his mind and self controlled, free of expectation and free of possessions.

sanskrit: śucau deśe pratiṣṭhāpya sthiram āsanam ātmanaḥ nātyucchritaṃ nātinīcaṃ cailājinakuśottaram
english: Setting up for himself in a clean place a firm seat, neither too high nor too low, covered with cloth, deerskin, and kuśa grass,

sanskrit: tatraikāgraṃ manaḥ kṛtvā yatacittendriyakriyaḥ upaviśyāsane yuñjyād yogam ātmaviśuddhaye
english: there, making the mind one-pointed, with the activity of thought and senses restrained, seated upon his seat, let him practice yoga for the purification of the self.

sanskrit: samaṃ kāyaśirogrīvaṃ dhārayann acalaṃ sthiraḥ saṃprekṣya nāsikāgraṃ svaṃ diśaś cānavalokayan
english: Holding body, head, and neck erect, motionless and steady, gazing at the tip of his own nose and not looking about in any direction,

sanskrit: praśāntātmā vigatabhīr brahmacārivrate sthitaḥ manaḥ saṃyamya maccitto yukta āsīta matparaḥ
english: his self tranquil, his fear gone, firm in the vow of chastity, restraining the mind, with his thought on Me, let him sit yoked, holding Me as the supreme.

sanskrit: yuñjann evaṃ sadātmānaṃ yogī niyatamānasaḥ śāntiṃ nirvāṇaparamāṃ matsaṃsthām adhigacchati
english: Thus ever yoking the self, the yogin of disciplined mind attains the peace that culminates in extinction and abides in Me.

sanskrit: nātyaśnatas tu yogo 'sti na caikāntam anaśnataḥ na cātisvapnaśīlasya jāgrato naiva cārjuna
english: Yoga is not for one who eats too much, nor for one who does not eat at all, nor for one given to too much sleep, nor again for one who keeps awake, O Arjuna.

sanskrit: yuktāhāravihārasya yuktaceṣṭasya karmasu yuktasvapnāvabodhasya yogo bhavati duḥkhahā
english: For one moderate in eating and recreation, moderate in his efforts at work, moderate in sleeping and waking, yoga becomes the destroyer of sorrow.

sanskrit: yadā viniyataṃ cittam ātmany evāvatiṣṭhate niḥspṛhaḥ sarvakāmebhyo yukta ity ucyate tadā
english: When the disciplined mind comes to rest in the self alone, free of longing for all desires, then one is said to be yoked.

sanskrit: yathā dīpo nivātastho neṅgate sopamā smṛtā yogino yatacittasya yuñjato yogam ātmanaḥ
english: As a lamp standing in a windless place does not flicker—that is the likeness remembered of the yogin of controlled mind, practicing the yoga of the self.

sanskrit: yatroparamate cittaṃ niruddhaṃ yogasevayā yatra caivātmanātmānaṃ paśyann ātmani tuṣyati
english: When the mind comes to rest, stilled by the practice of yoga, and when, beholding the self by the self, one is content within the self;

sanskrit: sukham ātyantikaṃ yat tad buddhigrāhyam atīndriyam vetti yatra na caivāyaṃ sthitaś calati tattvataḥ
english: when one knows that boundless happiness which is grasped by the intellect and lies beyond the senses, and, established there, this man no longer wavers from the truth;

sanskrit: yaṃ labdhvā cāparaṃ lābhaṃ manyate nādhikaṃ tataḥ yasmin sthito na duḥkhena guruṇāpi vicālyate
english: having gained which, he thinks no other gain greater than it, and, established in which, he is not shaken even by heavy sorrow—

sanskrit: taṃ vidyād duḥkhasaṃyogaviyogaṃ yogasaṃjñitam sa niścayena yoktavyo yogo 'nirviṇṇacetasā
english: let him know that disjunction from union with pain to be what is named yoga. That yoga is to be practiced with resolve and with an unwearied mind.

sanskrit: saṃkalpaprabhavān kāmāṃs tyaktvā sarvān aśeṣataḥ manasaivendriyagrāmaṃ viniyamya samantataḥ
english: Abandoning without remainder all desires born of selfish intention, and restraining the whole host of the senses on every side by the mind alone,

sanskrit: śanaiḥ śanair uparamed buddhyā dhṛtigṛhītayā ātmasaṃsthaṃ manaḥ kṛtvā na kiṃ cid api cintayet
english: little by little let him come to rest, by an intellect held firm in steadfastness; fixing the mind upon the self, let him not think of anything at all.

sanskrit: yato yato niścarati manaś cañcalam asthiram tatas tato niyamyaitad ātmany eva vaśaṃ nayet
english: Whenever and wherever the restless, unsteady mind wanders away, from there let him rein it in and bring it under the sway of the self alone.

sanskrit: praśāntamanasaṃ hy enaṃ yoginaṃ sukham uttamam upaiti śāntarajasaṃ brahmabhūtam akalmaṣam
english: For supreme happiness comes to this yogin whose mind is tranquil, whose passion is stilled, who has become Brahman and is free of stain.

sanskrit: yuñjann evaṃ sadātmānaṃ yogī vigatakalmaṣaḥ sukhena brahmasaṃsparśam atyantaṃ sukham aśnute
english: Thus ever yoking the self, the yogin freed from stain easily enjoys the boundless happiness of contact with Brahman.

sanskrit: sarvabhūtastham ātmānaṃ sarvabhūtāni cātmani īkṣate yogayuktātmā sarvatra samadarśanaḥ
english: His self yoked in yoga, seeing the same everywhere, he beholds the self abiding in all beings and all beings in the self.

sanskrit: yo māṃ paśyati sarvatra sarvaṃ ca mayi paśyati tasyāhaṃ na praṇaśyāmi sa ca me na praṇaśyati
english: He who sees Me everywhere and sees all things in Me—for him I am not lost, and he is not lost to Me.

sanskrit: sarvabhūtasthitaṃ yo māṃ bhajaty ekatvam āsthitaḥ sarvathā vartamāno 'pi sa yogī mayi vartate
english: The yogin who, established in oneness, worships Me as abiding in all beings—in whatever way he lives, that yogin lives in Me.

sanskrit: ātmaupamyena sarvatra samaṃ paśyati yo 'rjuna sukhaṃ vā yadi vā duḥkhaṃ sa yogī paramo mataḥ
english: He who, by the likeness of himself, sees the same everywhere, O Arjuna, whether it be pleasure or pain—that yogin is held to be the highest.

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca yo 'yaṃ yogas tvayā proktaḥ sāmyena madhusūdana etasyāhaṃ na paśyāmi cañcalatvāt sthitiṃ sthirām
english: Arjuna said: This yoga that you have declared to consist of equanimity, O slayer of Madhu—of it I do not see any stable foundation, because of the restlessness of the mind.

sanskrit: cañcalaṃ hi manaḥ kṛṣṇa pramāthi balavad dṛḍham tasyāhaṃ nigrahaṃ manye vāyor iva suduṣkaram
english: For the mind is restless, O Kṛṣṇa, turbulent, powerful, and obstinate; I think the restraining of it as hard to achieve as that of the wind.

sanskrit: śrībhagavān uvāca asaṃśayaṃ mahābāho mano durnigrahaṃ calam abhyāsena tu kaunteya vairāgyeṇa ca gṛhyate
english: The Blessed Lord said: Without doubt, O mighty-armed, the mind is hard to restrain and unsteady; yet by practice, O son of Kuntī, and by dispassion it is held in check.

sanskrit: asaṃyatātmanā yogo duṣprāpa iti me matiḥ vaśyātmanā tu yatatā śakyo 'vāptum upāyataḥ
english: By one whose self is unrestrained, yoga is hard to attain—such is My judgment; but by one whose self is mastered and who strives, it can be attained by the proper means.

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca ayatiḥ śraddhayopeto yogāc calitamānasaḥ aprāpya yogasaṃsiddhiṃ kāṃ gatiṃ kṛṣṇa gacchati
english: Arjuna said: One who does not strive, though endowed with faith, his mind fallen away from yoga, having failed to reach perfection in yoga—what path, O Kṛṣṇa, does he go to?

sanskrit: kaccin nobhayavibhraṣṭaś chinnābhram iva naśyati apratiṣṭho mahābāho vimūḍho brahmaṇaḥ pathi
english: Does he not, fallen from both, perish like a scattered cloud, O mighty-armed, without foundation and bewildered upon the path of Brahman?

sanskrit: etan me saṃśayaṃ kṛṣṇa chettum arhasy aśeṣataḥ tvad anyaḥ saṃśayasyāsya chettā na hy upapadyate
english: This doubt of mine, O Kṛṣṇa, you ought to cut away without remainder; for no other than you can be found to dispel this doubt.

sanskrit: śrībhagavān uvāca pārtha naiveha nāmutra vināśas tasya vidyate na hi kalyāṇakṛt kaś cid durgatiṃ tāta gacchati
english: The Blessed Lord said: O Pārtha, neither here nor in the world beyond is there any ruin for him; for no one who does good, my dear, comes to a sorry end.

sanskrit: prāpya puṇyakṛtāṃl lokān uṣitvā śāśvatīḥ samāḥ śucīnāṃ śrīmatāṃ gehe yogabhraṣṭo 'bhijāyate
english: Having attained the worlds of those who do meritorious deeds, and having dwelt there for endless years, the one fallen from yoga is born again in the house of the pure and the prosperous.

sanskrit: atha vā yoginām eva kule bhavati dhīmatām etad dhi durlabhataraṃ loke janma yad īdṛśam
english: Or else he comes to be born in the family of wise yogins; for such a birth as this is the more difficult to win in this world.

sanskrit: tatra taṃ buddhisaṃyogaṃ labhate paurvadehikam yatate ca tato bhūyaḥ saṃsiddhau kurunandana
english: There he regains that union with the understanding gained in his former body, and from there he strives onward once more toward perfection, O joy of the Kurus.

sanskrit: pūrvābhyāsena tenaiva hriyate hy avaśo 'pi saḥ jijñāsur api yogasya śabdabrahmātivartate
english: For by that very practice of his former life he is carried onward, even against his will; and merely seeking to know yoga, he passes beyond the Brahman of the word.

sanskrit: prayatnād yatamānas tu yogī saṃśuddhakilbiṣaḥ anekajanmasaṃsiddhas tato yāti parāṃ gatim
english: But the yogin who strives with effort, his stains thoroughly purified, perfected through many births, then attains the supreme goal.

sanskrit: tapasvibhyo 'dhiko yogī jñānibhyo 'pi mato 'dhikaḥ karmibhyaś cādhiko yogī tasmād yogī bhavārjuna
english: The yogin is greater than the ascetics, and held to be greater even than the men of knowledge, and the yogin is greater than the men of works; therefore become a yogin, O Arjuna.

sanskrit: yoginām api sarveṣāṃ madgatenāntarātmanā śraddhāvān bhajate yo māṃ sa me yuktatamo mataḥ
english: And of all yogins, he who worships Me full of faith, his inmost self gone forth to Me—him I hold to be the most deeply yoked.

sanskrit: śrībhagavān uvāca mayy āsaktamanāḥ pārtha yogaṃ yuñjan madāśrayaḥ asaṃśayaṃ samagraṃ māṃ yathā jñāsyasi tac chṛṇu
english: The Blessed Lord said: With your mind attached to Me, O Pārtha, practicing yoga and taking refuge in Me, hear how you shall know Me wholly and without doubt.
